chunks: Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Ibn Abi Umayr from Saif ibn Amirah from Mansur from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Ali (peace be upon him) used to say: 'When the son of al-mula'ana dies and he has brothers, his wealth is distributed according to the shares of Allah (i.e., the standard inheritance shares).'

key_terms.اِبْنُ اَلْمُلاَعَنَةِ: Son of al-mula'ana (child of a couple undergoing ritual declaration of non-paternity)
key_terms.سِهَامِ اَللَّهِ: Shares of Allah (standard Quranic inheritance portions)

ai.seo_question: How is the estate of the son of al-mula'ana distributed if he dies with siblings?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies that the 'son of al-mula'ana' inherits as a full heir rather than being excluded, with his estate distributed among siblings according to standard Quranic portions (*siham Allah*). This ruling highlights the Shia juristic view that the ritual of cursing establishes non-paternity for the father but does not sever the child's right to inherit from the maternal line or siblings, distinguishing it from the *lagn* (non-heir) status in some other schools.
